not_handled: The Windows version (SYSTEM3.EXE and its DLLs) on the same disk; the patch covers the DOS programs.

remarks: The 249 `name` entries, the verb/object captions, the engine strings and the title menu were translated by hand earlier (romanization of names without an official source, e.g. セイル = "Seil", is a guess).

**Output is a hard-disk image.** The scenario floppies hold about 1 MB of CG each and cannot fit a long English script, so `PATCH.BAT` installs the game the way its own HDD installer does (AD.BAT / B_COPY.BAT): system files in `\SG_SET2`, each scenario in `\SG_SET2\SNR1`-`SNR3`, the installer's `SET2A.ORG` as `\SET2.BAT`, scenario 1 as the default copy. The DOS setup comes from the collection's Super D.P.S hard-disk image (its own game is removed), so that image must be in the collection. It boots straight into scenario 1; to pick another, quit to DOS and type `SET2 2` or `SET2 3` (`SET2 ?` lists them).

remarks: This is Elf's 1989 build of ADVH, older than the Fairytale/Cocktail Soft ones: its `ADVH.EXE` is neither EXEPACK-packed nor wrapped, and is written back unpacked; it has no disk-change command, so the half-width helper is put after the end of its image (the end of the text loop's code segment) and the header's size grows with it; it draws its glyphs squeezed to ten rows (lines 11 dots apart), and the helper squeezes the letters the same way (`pc98tl/advh.py`).

The main disk is Elf's own boot disk: FAT with no BPB in its boot sector, read with the standard 2HD layout (`pc98tl/disk.py`); its `ELF1.SYS`/`ELF2.SYS` system is not installed (the hard disk's DOS runs the game).
Scripts are loaded at DS:D800h and run up to the code segment at 1200h, a 10240-byte buffer (`script_room`).
The startup script's procedure 1 clears the box and shows a scene picture; it is not taken as the message end (a procedure that loads a file never is), and pages are split with the key wait `81 90`.

The speech boxes are set by the start script's subroutine 1, which picks one of four windows by a variable the scene sets just before calling it (`0A var n`); the patcher follows the start script's subroutines into every scene and takes the window the variable picks (`pc98tl/ai5.py` windows).
The party's names are typed in the name entry (its kana grid stays Japanese) and printed by subroutines 16-18; the patcher keeps 8 cells for each.

Monster and item names in battle come from `SENTO.COM`, a table of 30-byte records, each with a 12-byte name field ended by a NUL: `r` ids, written in full-width letters, up to `max_cells` (5) letters.

The battle prints a name (command 14) and a number (command 15) between the pieces of its one-line messages; the patcher counts 10 cells for each (game.json "inserts": the longest monster name, five full-width letters, and a five-digit number in full-width digits), so the text after them wraps and pages from where they leave the line.

Subroutines 7 and 8 print the hero's family and given name from the name entry (its kana grid stays Japanese; the defaults はつしば and りゅうすけ are poked by OPEN.MES); the patcher keeps 12 cells for each.  Subroutine 9 prints an ellipsis (three ・) in Japanese; 6 cells.  Subroutines 18, 21 and 22 (083.MES) print an island's, a place's and a guide's name, their text strings of their own; 16 cells each.
The speaker tags (【...】) are subroutine bodies the script defines in a table (12 n, the text), which the driver treats as menu items: full-width letters within the Japanese tag's width.
The boot test stops at the first menu: np21w passes no key or mouse input that picks an item, in the original game too (AUTOEXEC.BAT loads Elf's ELF.COM, and START.MES the mouse cursor MOUSE.DAT).

The --pseudo build cuts its filler to fit the 64 KB script segment: DOR2.EDT by 2,266 letters, DOR3.EDT (48,032 bytes in Japanese) by 19,182 and DOR4B.EDT by 7,206; a real translation must keep those scripts about as long in bytes as the Japanese plus what the segment leaves (the patcher refuses and names the strings otherwise).
DOR has English Windows releases (DOR Package Edition / Download Edition, VNDB): another platform, linked for the translation role to port from; it does not block this patch.
Part 1's ADL.EXE is an earlier build than Part 2's (its data segment at 474h, its variables a byte lower, no key-skip in the character wait); the patch reads every address off the program.
DOR has an English Windows release (G-Collections 2002; VNDB lists the Package and Download Editions): another platform, linked for the translation role to port from; it does not block this patch.
Scenario 1 is a chain of scripts (S01_A to S01_N, each loading the next with 50h); a script that draws text before it sets a window uses the one its loader set, which the patcher follows.
